title: Prove N(c) ≥ ⌊5c/2⌋ for the unsigned connector via five-source depth-two blocks in every c ≥ 5 (no new κ)
body:
## Result

For the unsigned dirty connector of #4231 in characteristic c, let N(c) be the largest source count at which the floor c(k + 2^k − 1) is attained. #4248 proved N(c) ≥ 2c and asked how N(c) grows (open question 2). This PR adds `research/connector-five-halves-growth`:

- **Theorem T (scoped proof, finite core checked):** one explicit 30-event base walk with per-source cut positions expands to a five-source depth-two block in every characteristic c ≥ 5. Replace the (a_j+1)-th event of source j by a run of c − 5 copies (deleted at c = 5). Each expanded prefix is congruent mod c to an integer "lifted" prefix, and every nonzero mask is an integer sum of two lifted prefixes, so the identity holds in every c ≥ 5.
- **Corollary (proof):** with #4248's concatenation and deletion lemmas, **N(c) ≥ ⌊5c/2⌋ for every c ≥ 5**, for example N(5) ≥ 12, N(6) ≥ 15, N(7) ≥ 17 and N(8) ≥ 20 (previously 2c).

Characteristic four is untouched. #4271 excludes five-source depth-two blocks at c = 4, and the template needs c − 5 ≥ 0. There is no new κ, no consumer, no selected-frontier change and no multiplication theorem.

## Evidence and reproduction

`verify.py` uses only the standard library and takes about 2 s. It checks:

- the integer template identity for all 31 masks (the only finite step the proof needs);
- the expanded block for every 5 ≤ c ≤ 64, by direct search modulo c and through the lifted readouts;
- literal floor words on 12, 15 and 17 sources for c = 5, 6, 7 (20,535, 196,692 and 917,616 calls), simulated with generic coefficients over Z/c;
- five rejection controls.

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/connector-five-halves-growth/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/connector-five-halves-growth/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/connector-five-halves-growth
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/connector-five-halves-growth --check-source-history
```

All four passed locally (CPython 3.12, macOS). Marker: `PASS_CONNECTOR_FIVE_HALVES depth_two_k5_every_c>=5 N(c)>=floor(5c/2)`. Both registered VERIFY.json commands take about 1.5 s each.

## Limitations

- Only the unsigned, immutable-source, complete-call interface of #4231. The prefix criterion, concatenation lemma and deletion lemma are cited from #4248/#4232 and not re-derived.
- Theorem T is proved for every c ≥ 5. The direct block check covers c ≤ 64 and the literal word simulation c ≤ 7.
- N(c) for c ≥ 5 remains open between ⌊5c/2⌋ and the counting bound. No physical consumer or call pricing is supplied.
- Proof-kernel checks and independent human review are not claimed.

## Open next questions

1. Does any characteristic admit a depth-two block on six or more sources? One valid for all large c would give N(c) ≥ 3c.
2. Is there a depth-three block on eight or more sources valid for every large c (density 8/3 > 5/2)?
3. Is N(c)/c unbounded? Counting gives O(c log c).
4. Does any concrete consumer use a characteristic-c batch at a favorable complete invoice?

## Related open work

- #4079, #3909 and #3897 study other connector variants (weight-at-most-four outputs, arity-four calls, joint-output charges). None studies N(c) or depth blocks; no shared number.

- #6037 studies balanced multiplicities of the depth-three chain connector (#4257), a different connector object from the unsigned all-mask connector here; no shared number.

No open PR studies N(c) or depth-two blocks.

## Credit

Builds on #4231 (interface, floor), #4248 (prefix criterion, depth, concatenation and deletion lemmas, N(c) ≥ 2c, open question), #4232 (deletion lemma), #4255 (counting bound) and #4271 (c = 4 depth-two obstruction). Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19230522
